summary: Strong risk-on momentum following a 6-day winning streak off the Aug 5 lows, fueled by blowout retail sales (+1.0% vs +0.3% expected), falling jobless claims, and CPI at 2.9%. Rally is extended approaching July highs—mean reversion and selective momentum plays appropriate in range-bound regime.

sections.title: Macro
sections.content: July retail sales surged 1.0% MoM (consensus +0.3%), easing recession fears that drove the Aug 5 selloff. Weekly jobless claims fell to 227K (vs 235K est). CPI annual rate hit 2.9%, lowest since Mar 2021, cementing September rate cut expectations. Housing starts data due Aug 16 AM will show -6.8% to 1.2M annualized rate (weakest since May 2020). UMich preliminary consumer sentiment at 67.8, essentially flat. Macro picture is goldilocks: strong consumer, cooling inflation, labor market holding.

sections.title: Corporate
sections.content: Walmart Q2 beat: EPS $0.67 vs $0.65, revenue $169.3B vs $168.6B, comp sales +4.2%, general merch positive first time in 11 quarters, raised FY guidance. Deere beat EPS ($6.29 vs $5.80) but revenue down 17% YoY to $13.15B. Applied Materials reported after close Aug 15: beat EPS $2.12 vs $2.01 and revenue $6.78B (+1.63% surprise). Target earnings upcoming Aug 21.

sections.title: Technicals
sections.content: S&P 500 at ~5,555 area on a 6-day win streak, recovered ~8% from Aug 5 intraday low. V-shaped recovery approaching July highs. RSI overbought on shorter timeframes. VIX collapsed from Aug 5 spike (38+) back to low-teens. Bitcoin stuck at $57-59K, below $60K resistance. Silver rallied 2.8% on Aug 15 to $28.36.

scenarios.trade: AMAT beat on both top and bottom lines in a strong semi environment. The AI capex narrative gets another confirmation datapoint—if companies are spending more on semiconductor equipment, the entire AI supply chain thesis strengthens. With the broader market in risk-on mode, NVDA rallying, and positive macro data, AMAT should see post-earnings momentum. The stock closed at $208.58 before the after-hours print. Target $217 represents a 4.0% move vs 2.2% stop = 1.84:1 R:R, with the post-earnings gap-up dynamic front-loading the move.

scenarios.implication: Market already extended on 6-day streak—profit taking could cap upside. Semi stocks may face sell-the-news reaction if forward guidance language was cautious. Housing starts weakness at 9:30 AM release could briefly weigh on sentiment.

scenarios.trade: TGT reports earnings Aug 21—just 3 trading days away. Walmart's beat and the retail sales surge create a powerful one-two catalyst for TGT's pre-earnings positioning. The consumer is clearly spending (retail sales +1.0% vs +0.3% expected), and WMT noted general merchandise turning positive—which is TGT's core strength area. TGT has underperformed WMT, creating catch-up potential. Target $137.50 = 3.9% upside, stop $129.30 = 2.3% downside, giving 1.7:1 R:R. This is a swing trade into the earnings catalyst window.

scenarios.implication: WMT may have taken market share FROM TGT rather than signaling broad retail strength. TGT has underperformed for company-specific reasons that may persist. Holding into earnings is risky if TGT misses. The pre-earnings premium may already be baked in after the Aug 15 rally.

scenarios.trade: NVDA is the AI bellwether recovering from the Aug 5 selloff. AMAT's beat on semi capex spending provides a direct positive read-through—if companies are spending more on semiconductor equipment, NVDA's datacenter GPU demand thesis strengthens further. With earnings Aug 28, institutional positioning typically begins 2 weeks out. The goldilocks macro (strong consumer + cooling inflation) supports growth/momentum names. Target 3.7% upside vs 2.2% downside = 1.7:1 R:R.

scenarios.implication: NVDA has already rallied hard off the Aug 5 lows and may consolidate near the $125 resistance level (July breakdown area). Broader market profit-taking after a 6-day streak could weigh. Housing starts data could inject caution at the open. The Aug 28 earnings are still 2 weeks out—timing risk on a day trade.

scenarios.trade: BA has been one of the most beaten-down large-caps in 2024 due to quality/safety issues and trades well below historical range. The Aug 15 surge (+3.8%) on retail sales data signals institutional buying as recession fears recede. In a range-bound regime with slight bullish bias, buying into a beaten-down name that just broke above near-term resistance with volume is a solid momentum continuation setup. Defense spending tailwinds add secular support. Target $183.50 = 4.0% upside, stop $173.10 = 1.9% downside = 2.1:1 R:R.

scenarios.implication: BA-specific operational risks remain (FAA scrutiny, 737 MAX production limits). Extended 6-day winning streak in indices increases odds of a consolidation day. Weak housing starts data could weigh on industrial sentiment. Weak housing starts data could weigh on industrial sentiment broadly.

scenarios.trade: DE surged 3.9% on Aug 15 despite a 17% revenue decline—classic cost-cut-driven EPS beat that masks fundamental weakness. Agricultural equipment cycle is in clear downturn with worldwide net sales declining sharply. FY24 outlook was cut. In a range-bound regime, this kind of relief rally on a deteriorating top line is a textbook mean-reversion short. Housing starts data due Aug 16 (very weak at -6.8%) reinforces the narrative that capital equipment/construction spending is slowing. Target $352 = 3.4% downside, stop $372.60 = 2.2% upside risk = 1.5:1 R:R.

scenarios.implication: Broad market momentum could continue lifting all boats including DE. The EPS beat was substantial and cost discipline may be genuinely underappreciated by the market. Short-covering and momentum chasers could push the stock higher. Overall bullish market bias works against shorts.

watchlist: COIN - Crypto/bitcoin plays if BTC breaks above $60K resistance; currently range-bound at $57-59K. No clear catalyst for breakout today.
MARA - Same crypto thesis as COIN, higher beta. Needs BTC directional move to trigger entry.
SLV - Silver momentum with precious metals bid; silver closed at $28.36 up 2.8% on Aug 15. Watching for continuation but extended after the move.
WMT - Strong earnings beat but stock already ran on the results. Watching for pullback entry on any profit-taking.
avoidList: TSLA - Up 4.4% on Aug 15 to $214.14, extended after recovery rally with no near-term fundamental catalyst. High beta risk in an already-extended market. Better to wait for consolidation.
Homebuilders (XHB, DHI, LEN) - Housing starts data due Aug 16 AM expected very weak (-6.8%, lowest since May 2020). Potential negative sector catalyst despite rate cut hopes.
Small-cap value (IWM) - While economic data is strong, the Aug recovery has been led by mega-cap tech. Small caps may lag if market consolidates from overbought levels.
